draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row '(default)' overlaid with the frontage row: The Robbins house (Mann, MacNeille & Lindeberg) RISING on 1 July 1904, in the one working phase census ruling r35-robbins-2126 declares: the brick shell two storeys up over its stone basement, the street wall and its returns 1.6 m into the third, openings empty, no roof, a deck at the principal floor and a pole scaffold along the street and the open side. The five-bay front and central entrance are the register's for the finished house (its 'five-bay red-brick front ... fanlit central entry'), laid out as openings only. The May 1905 plate is the finished design and is not read as July 1904 evidence; a 1904 permit or a dated progress photograph replaces this phase (T-1926). Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 2929825281 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3 brick dwelling (D), the Robbins house'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (phase_unresolved). On the target date the house is not finished (census ruling r35-robbins-2126): Robbins bought the Hamill house in 1901 and razed it in 1904, and the May 1905 plate shows the new house complete. The draft therefore stands the working phase the ruling declares, the new house's brick shell partly raised and unroofed on the 1911 footprint, with the alley stable standing. How high the walls stood is RECONSTRUCTED: two of its three storeys and part of the third along the street.
